behaviours.comparison: S2 endorsed without a mandatory sales stop above 5% (weakened: above-limit sales must stop); S5 endorsed with recall left to regulator discretion rather than a mandatory numeric recall (weakened). Both weakenings are endorsed together as a package, with each side's loosened section tied to the other's.
behaviours.excerpt: The current text appropriately treats the 5% test level as a corrective-action and retesting trigger, not an automatic ban, and makes model-specific results available to customers. Likewise, exceeding 8 incidents per 100,000 should trigger regulator notification and investigation, with a recall required when the evidence shows imminent serious risk or other measures cannot adequately reduce risk.

S1_incident_reporting.quote: Manufacturers must report to the relevant regulator any battery thermal incident involving overheating, fire, smoke, or thermal runaway within 24 hours of learning of it, with a fuller incident report within 10 business days. Manufacturers must notify the affected customer within 24 hours when an incident involves their unit, and promptly provide safety instructions and any known risk to nearby occupants.

S2_thermal_testing.quote: A failure rate above 5% requires the manufacturer to submit a corrective-action plan and retest schedule to the relevant regulator. Regulators may require corrective action, retesting, or sales restrictions based on the test results and associated safety evidence. Individual-company per-model failure rates are not required to be published to the general public.

S3_remote_shutoff.quote: New units placed on the market must support remote emergency shut-off by 1 January 2028, with safeguards against unauthorized activation and clear customer instructions. Existing installed units must be brought into compliance, where technically feasible, within six years of this standard taking effect; manufacturers must provide customers with a retrofit plan and disclose units that cannot be retrofitted.

S4_fire_suppression.quote: New home battery units must include built-in fire suppression no earlier than 36 months after adoption of this standard. Until the requirement takes effect, manufacturers must disclose whether each model includes built-in suppression and describe other fire-mitigation measures.

S5_customer_disclosure.quote: When a model exceeds 8 thermal incidents per 100,000 installed units in a year, the manufacturer must promptly notify regulators, investigate and submit verified incident data and a corrective-action plan, and notify affected customers. A recall is mandatory when a model exceeds that annual threshold.

document.section_notes: S2 contains no permanent sales limit: the 5% figure only triggers a corrective-action plan and retesting, and regulators may restrict sales at their discretion. S5 makes recall mandatory above 8 per 100,000 with no transition period, which applies to Halcyon's Ember 8 at 9.9 and is the main cost to Halcyon. S4 delays built-in suppression to no earlier than 36 months, which favours Halcyon's higher suppression cost, while S3 gives a six-year retrofit window that favours Northwind's 38% shut-off coverage.
